title: Dusting horizontal blinds without leaving streaks
audience: Cleaners who dust horizontal blinds in offices, reception areas and short-stay units.
learningOutcomes: Set a horizontal blind into the correct position for dusting both faces of each slat.
Dust the room-facing and window-facing sides of the slats in a planned sequence.
Check a blind at an angle and correct any dust line that remains.

instruction.heading: Why blinds need a set method
instruction.body: Horizontal slats collect dust on both faces. A single pass leaves a line on the face you missed, which shows as a streak once light hits the blind. Dust both faces of every slat in a planned sequence so each face is covered once.

instruction.heading: Setting up the blind
instruction.body: Lower the blind fully. Angle the slats so they face slightly downward, into the room. Use a short-handled duster, static or microfiber, since a long handle makes the slats harder to control.

instruction.heading: The two passes
instruction.body: First, dust the room-facing side in one sweep, beginning at the top rail and moving downward, working across the width as you go. Second, ease the bottom rail away from the window, turn the slats the other way using the tilting control, and dust the window-facing side from the bottom rail upward. Angle the slats before each pass so the duster meets every face square-on.

instruction.heading: Why streaks form and how to catch them
instruction.body: A streak appears when a face is skipped, or when a slat is dusted in the wrong direction and dust rolls onto the next slat. After finishing, look at the blind from a slight angle. If a line is visible, go back over that slat with the duster.

procedure: Put on protective equipment and check the blind is clean at its top rail.
Lower the blind fully and angle the slats downward into the room.
Dust the room-facing side from the head rail downward with a short-handled duster.
Pull the bottom rail gently away from the glass, tilt the slats, and dust the window-facing side from the bottom upward.
Check the blind at a slight angle and re-dust any line that remains.

workedExamples.situation: After cleaning, a blind shows fine dust lines on every third slat.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the likely cause, and what should be done?
workedExamples.reasoning: Those slats were skipped on one face, or were dusted in the wrong direction and pushed dust onto the next slat. Re-dust the marked slats on both faces using the two-pass method. Use a clean duster so the dust is not spread again.

commonErrors.error: Dusting one face of the slats only.
commonErrors.prevention: Use both passes so each face of every slat is covered.

commonErrors.error: Dusting with the slats at the wrong angle.
commonErrors.prevention: Angle the slats before starting each pass.

commonErrors.error: Using a damp duster on dry dust, which smears it.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a dry static duster or a dry microfiber duster.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Work from a stable step or a safe reach. Do not climb onto the window sill.
Handle the cords and the bottom rail gently; pulling hard can damage the blind or tangle the cords.

qualityStandard: Both faces of every slat have been dusted.
No visible lines remain when the blind is viewed at a slight angle.
The blind is returned to its usual position.
documentationEvidence: Blind dusting logged on the route sheet.
summary: Dust both faces of every slat in two planned passes.
Angle the slats before each pass, and check the blind from a slight angle.
Re-dust any line at once with a dry duster.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must both faces of a slat be dusted?
options: Because dust sits on both faces, and a missed face shows as a line
Because the client counts the slats and each one must be right
Because blinds are usually damp from the air conditioning

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a blind be positioned before the first pass?
options: Fully raised and open so the light comes in across the whole room
Fully lowered, with the slats angled downward into the room
Half lowered, with the slats angled upward toward the ceiling

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best check after dusting a blind?
options: Press the slats flat and check them by feel only today
Wipe each slat once with a dry cloth and move on quickly
Look at the blind from a slight angle for any remaining line
